title: Billing Analyst Worked-Example Sheet: Collection Recovery on Transferred Electric Service Agreement Balances
content:
**Electric Service Agreement.** A collection recovery is added to the transfer amount when the unpaid balance of a closed agreement is transferred. It is set by the written disconnection notices served on the closed agreement in the 12 calendar months before the transfer:

- two or more written disconnection notices: 1.2 times the schedule's returned payment fee;
- exactly one written disconnection notice: 0.6 times the schedule's returned payment fee;
- none: nothing.

The schedule is the closed agreement's schedule. The collection recovery is added to the closed agreement's balance before the transfer amount is rounded to the cent.

Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date; the posting here is the transfer.

## Worked examples (all inputs hypothetical)

Hypothetical returned payment fee on the closed agreement's schedule: USD 25.00.

| Example | Written notices in the look-back | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | 1.2 times 25.00, USD 30.00 |
| B | 2 | 1.2 times 25.00, USD 30.00 |
| C | 1 | 0.6 times 25.00, USD 15.00 |
| D | 0 | USD 0.00 |

**Example E (window edge).** Transfer dated 15 September. One written disconnection notice dated 15 September of the previous year (exactly 12 whole calendar months earlier, not counted) and one dated 2 February of the transfer year (counted): one notice counts, so the recovery is 0.6 times the fee, USD 15.00.

**Example F (window edge).** Same transfer, notices dated 16 September of the previous year and 2 February: both are less than 12 whole calendar months earlier, so two notices count and the recovery is USD 30.00.
